Subject: Streamline AI: ops constraints & SLO alignment (post-call)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get an accurate ops/price fit for Streamline AI. I captured the items we talked through; please flag anything I missed or mischaracterized.

Key pain points you shared
- Spiky inference traffic (batch of users during report generation windows, ~10x baseline for ~15–30 minutes).
- Needs P95 end-to-end latency under 1s for short prompts (50–200 tokens) and P99 under 2.5s when load is steady.
- Cost sensitivity: primary goal is predictable unit economics for peak periods to avoid runaway GPU spend.
- Regulatory: logs and audit trail retention for 12 months (HIPAA adjacent workflow).

Goals we agreed on
- Validate a production topology that holds P95 <1s for interactive UI flows at expected peak QPS.
- Identify model/quantization profile to get 3–4x cost reduction vs baseline while staying within quality budget.
- Produce a mutual action plan (MAP) that includes a 2-week PoC window and SLA targets for go/no-go.

Technical surface points we discussed
- Current request mix: ~65% short interactive prompts (avg 120 tokens), 25% medium (300–600 tokens), 10% long-batch.
- Target peak concurrent inference: ~450 concurrent requests for interactive flow.
- Existing infra: you run a node pool on GCP us-west1; you cannot expose customer data outside your VPC for the PoC.
- KV/prefix caching is desirable: many users start with the same system prompt and small state.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) You to share a 48-hour sample of API logs (headers redacted) + 95/99 latency snapshots and representative prompt samples (we can accept a 1–2MB gzip).
2) We schedule a technical deep-dive with Redwood infra/serving (30–45 min) to map topology options and quantify expected instance counts under different batching and quantization strategies.
3) We will produce an SLO/ops sketch (initial capacity model + cost estimate) within 3 business days after receiving logs.

Attachments: streamline-postcall-notes.pdf (summary slides), sample-api-traffic.txt (example request traces), redwood-sla-sketch.png (early sketch)

If that looks right, can we lock the technical deep-dive for sometime next week? I have availability Tue/Wed mornings PDT.

Best,
Jonas

3) Do you have a recommended model family (Llama variant vs Mistral style) for our workload where the quality delta on short prompts is negligible but cost is lower?

Thanks for the loop-in, Jonas. Read the logs — good signal. Quick technical plan below; happy to expand during the deep-dive.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Topology: Private-peered Redwood Private control plane + customer-managed inference nodes in Streamline's GCP us-west1 project. This minimizes data egress and keeps audit/logs under their retention policy. Minimal networking work: a VPC peering and an IAM service account with limited permissions.
- Model family: start with a 13B open LLM that has a verified Redwood performance profile (we recommend a Llama-variant 13B FP16 baseline, with a 4-bit quantized variant for cost testing). For most short prompts the quality delta should be negligible; we will include a small A/B set to validate.
- Capacity estimates (rough): using Redwood serving profiles (avg 120 tokens, decode temp 0.0, streaming disabled):
  a) FP16 baseline: ~40 concurrent requests per A100-80GB equiv (sustained), so peak 550 qps would need ~14 GPUs (with 20% headroom).
  b) 8-bit quant: ~1.6x throughput improvement -> ~9 GPUs (20% headroom).
  c) 4-bit quant (aggressive): ~2.8x throughput improvement -> ~5 GPUs (20% headroom), but expect small quality delta on adversarial prompts.

- Prefix/KV caching impact: For short, similar-start prompts, enabling prefix/KV caching reduces token work by ~30–45% for Streamline's traffic profile. In practice, this reduces required GPUs by ~1.2x (i.e., FP16 baseline drops from 14 -> ~12). It's very effective when many requests share the same system prompt and initial tokens.

- Batching strategy: continuous batching with adaptive max-latency windows (10–30ms) to preserve P95. For interactive flow we bias batching for latency (lower window) and for long-batch we allow larger windows.

Operational notes for VPC-peered PoC:
- We can run inference nodes in their project as a managed node pool; Redwood provides an agent image. Required: a service account that can create/monitor instances, and a VPC peering route table entry.
- Logs: we can ship structured audit logs to their Cloud Logging; Redwood will still retain a minimal control-plane trace within our management network, encrypted at rest.

Deliverables for Tue deep-dive (20 Apr 09:00 PDT):
1) Walkthrough of topology and capacity sketch (I'll present numbers above).
2) Cost delta scenarios (FP16 vs 8-bit vs 4-bit) with estimated monthly run rates at their current baseline and projected peak windows.
3) Quick A/B validation plan for prompt-level quality checks (we'll bring a 200-sample set).
4) MAP draft: 2-week PoC with a 72-hour load test in week 2.

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet tomorrow with the GPU sizing and cost assumptions.

If that aligns with you, Jonas, please confirm I'll present these items and I'll add a short slide for ops steps.

—Karthik
